name: terms_title_doubling
why: Spec: 'score = competency weight × min(hits, 3) × (2 if in_title else 1), rounded to 4 decimals.' 'python' matches 3× in the jd (Python, python, PYTHON) and matches the title 'Python Developer' → 1.0 × min(3,3) × 2 = 6.0.
title: Python Developer

name: terms_three_hit_cap
why: Spec: 'min(hits, 3)'. 'sql' appears 5 times but hits are capped at 3; no title match → 1.5 × 3 × 1 = 4.5.
title: Data Engineer

name: terms_tie_alphabetical
why: Both clusters: hits 1, score 1.0 × min(1,3) × 1 = 1.0. Spec: 'Sort by score descending, then hits descending, then term alphabetically' → aws before docker.

name: terms_whole_token_llm_not_llmops
why: Spec: 'letters/digits around it break the match: "LLM" does not match "LLMOps"'. So 'LLMOps' and 'LLMs' do not count; only the standalone 'LLM' (1 hit). The title 'LLMOps Engineer' likewise contains no standalone 'LLM' → in_title false → 1.0 × 1 × 1 = 1.0. The 'rag' cluster has 0 hits and is skipped.
jd: LLMOps pipelines. LLMs at scale. One LLM here.
title: LLMOps Engineer

name: terms_spelling_tie_longer_wins
why: Spec: 'jd_spelling = the spelling with the most matches (ties → the longer spelling).' postgres 1 match, postgresql 1 match (whole-token: 'postgres' inside 'postgresql' does not count) → tie → 'postgresql' (10 chars) beats 'postgres' (8). hits = 2 → 1.0 × min(2,3) × 1 = 2.0.

name: terms_synonyms_sum_hits_most_matched_spelling
why: Spec: 'count = for each spelling, how many times it matches in the jd; hits = their sum.' k8s = 2, kubernetes = 1, kube = 0 (not a whole token of 'kubernetes') → hits 3, jd_spelling 'k8s' (most matches). No title → 1.0 × min(3,3) × 1 = 3.0.

name: terms_n_limit_keeps_first_two
why: All three clusters: hits 1, score 1.0 × 1 × 1 = 1.0, ordered alphabetically (ansible, bash, chef). Spec: 'keep the first n' with n=2 → only ansible and bash.

name: terms_score_tie_broken_by_hits
why: golang: 2 hits × 1.0 = 2.0; ansible: 1 hit × 2.0 = 2.0. Scores tie, so 'then hits descending' puts golang (2 hits) first even though 'ansible' is alphabetically first.
jd: Ansible playbooks. Golang services, golang workers.

name: parse_company_first_part_with_12_char_truncation
why: Spec: 'key = the folder's last path part, lower-cased, with a leading "YYYY-MM-DD_" removed' → key = acme_corp_international. 'The company is the first part p for which key starts with the first 12 characters of slug(p)': slug('Backend Engineer') → first 12 = 'backend_engi' (no), slug('Acme Corp International') → first 12 = 'acme_corp_in' (yes). Title = remaining parts joined with ' — '.
text:
# Backend Engineer — Acme Corp International — Remote

We build things.

name: parse_company_middle_part
why: key = 'hooli' (date prefix removed, lower-cased). slug('Platform Engineer') first 12 = 'platform_engi' → no; slug('Hooli') = 'hooli' → key starts with it → company is the middle part. Title joins the remaining parts.

name: parse_no_match_falls_back_to_last_part
why: key = 'umbrella' (no date prefix to strip) matches no part's slug prefix, so 'if none ... the last part' applies → company = 'Austin'; title = the remaining parts joined with ' — '.

name: parse_no_folder_last_part
why: Spec: 'if none (or no folder), the last part.' With an empty folder there is no key, so company = 'Vandelay Industries' and title = 'DevOps Engineer'.

name: parse_single_part_empty_company
why: Spec: 'With one part: (that part, "").' There is no ' — ' in the heading, so title is the whole part and company is empty, even though the folder would match.

name: parse_en_dash_does_not_split
why: Spec: 'Split the rest on " — " (an em dash with spaces; an en dash "–" ... does NOT split).' So the parts are ['Senior Engineer – Platform', 'Acme']; the en dash stays inside the title. slug('Acme') = 'acme' matches key 'acme'.

name: parse_hyphen_does_not_split
why: Spec: a hyphen does NOT split. Parts are ['Full-Stack Developer', 'Acme']; the hyphen is preserved in the title and slug('Full-Stack Developer') = 'full_stack_developer' (first 12 'full_stack_d') does not match key 'acme', while slug('Acme') does.

name: parse_no_hash_space_line
why: Spec: 'Take the first line starting with "# "' and 'No "# " line → ("", "")'. The line starts with '#B', not '# ', so there is no heading at all.
text:
#Backend Engineer — Acme Corp

No proper heading here.

name: tailor_acronym_swap_kubernetes_to_k8s
why: Term 'kubernetes' is true (fact f1, resume_ok true, entry on_resume true, skill 'Kubernetes'). jd_spelling is 'k8s' (3 jd matches) and is not on the page, while the other spelling 'Kubernetes' is in a bullet; 'is_bullet_variant (same words up to case / hyphens, or acronym ↔ expansion, with the same grammatical number)' allows the acronym swap → 'Managed k8s clusters across regions'. Headline: 'title, then up to 3 jd_spellings of true terms that are true skills and are not inside the title' → 'SRE · k8s'.
jd: k8s k8s at scale with strong k8s background
title: SRE

name: tailor_plural_pair_must_not_swap
why: Term 'workflow' is true via fact skill 'Workflows'. jd_spelling 'workflow' is not on the page and the page holds 'workflows', but spec says '"workflow"/"workflows" is NOT allowed', so no bullet change is recorded. No skill is added because jd_spelling 'workflow' is not a true skill ('Workflows' ≠ 'workflow' ignoring case), and the headline gets no additions.
title: Automation Engineer

bullets.text: Automated CI workflows with GitHub Actions

expect_first_bullets.e1: Automated CI workflows with GitHub Actions

name: tailor_not_true_term_never_added
why: No fact with resume_ok not false has a 'Terraform' skill and it is not in skills.not_true, so its truth is 'not true'. Spec: 'Never: ... a term that is not true.' Its jd_spelling is absent from the page but nothing is added; the headline gets no additions (it is not a true skill).
title: Platform Engineer

name: tailor_not_used_tool_never_swapped
why: No fact skill matches a spelling; 'Kubernetes' is in skills.not_true → truth is 'not used', not 'true'. A swap requires 'a true term whose jd_spelling is not on the page but another spelling s of the cluster is', so the page's 'Kubernetes' is left alone and nothing is added.
title: DevOps Engineer

name: tailor_skill_added_graphql
why: 'GraphQL' is true via the resume_ok fact's skills and its jd_spelling 'GraphQL' is not on the page (headline + summary + skills items + bullet texts) and is itself a true skill, so spec: 'is appended to one skills group'. Headline: 'title, then up to 3 jd_spellings of true terms that are true skills and are not inside the title' → 'API Engineer · GraphQL'.
title: API Engineer

name: tailor_headline_title_exclusion_and_cap
why: jd_terms order is score/hits/alphabetical → Docker, Kafka, Kubernetes, Redis, Terraform (all 3 hits, weight 1.0). Kubernetes is a true skill but sits inside the title (case-insensitive), so it is excluded; only the first 3 remaining qualify → 'Senior Kubernetes Engineer · Docker · Kafka · Redis' (Terraform dropped by the 3 cap). Every jd_spelling is already on the page, so nothing is swapped or added.
jd: Docker Docker Docker Kubernetes Kubernetes Kubernetes Kafka Kafka Kafka Redis Redis Redis Terraform Terraform Terraform
title: Senior Kubernetes Engineer
